title: Kinds of poem
hookLine: a playlist mixes love songs, chants and rap verses; the Granth holds many kinds of poem too
tomorrow: who catches the sounds you get wrong?
last: THE SMALL SIGNS · SMALL MARKS MATTER.

lines: A PLAYLIST ISN'T ONE KIND OF SONG.
A BALLAD, A STAIR, A COUPLET.
cards: Scroll through any long playlist and the songs aren't all one kind. A slow love song, a chant, a story told in verses, a short sharp line that gets stuck in your head. Nobody calls those the same thing.
The Granth is like that. The hymns aren't one shape poured out over and over. There's a ballad, there's a stair, there's a couplet, and the page tells you which one you're in.

teach.h: SHABAD: A HYMN WITH A CENTER.
teach.b: Six names to know, lightly. A shabad is a hymn, usually with a rahao at its center: most of what you've read this week.
An ashtpadi is a longer hymn of several verses; the Sukhmani is built from them. A chhant is a song form with a lyrical flow.
A var is a ballad, and it's made of pauris. The word pauri also means a step on a stair, and the Japji climbs pauri by pauri.
A salok is a short verse, often a couplet. In a var like the Asa di Var, saloks sit before the pauris, so a reading moves salok, salok, pauri, like voices answering each other.
And each form asks something different of you. A shabad asks you to find its center. A var asks you to hear a conversation.
A salok asks you to carry one short line all day. Here's the thing to tell someone tonight: the Granth isn't one long hymn on repeat.
It's many forms, each telling you how to listen.

how: The Guru Granth Sahib gathers many poetic forms, shabads, ashtpadis, chhants, vars of pauris with saloks, and readers and kirtan singers follow each form's shape, as in the morning singing of the Asa di Var.

games.q: at the gurdwara, the screen shows a salok, another salok, then a pauri, then saloks again. your friend whispers that the reader has lost his place. what's going on?
o: it's a var: saloks sit before each pauri, by design.
the reader skipped a page and is going back to fix it.
salok and pauri are two names for the same kind of verse.
games.why: in a var like the Asa di Var, saloks come before the pauris. the back-and-forth is the form, not a mistake.

practice: On paper, or with a fingertip on your palm, write the names of two forms you've read: maybe shabad and pauri. Under each, write one word for how it felt to read.
Then set the pen down, breathe slowly, and let the two words sit side by side.

wordCard.voice: Kinds of poem: the forms of the Granth, shabad, ashtpadi, chhant, var, pauri and salok, each a different way a hymn is built. The ninth word of the year.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: pauri, a stanza of a var or of the Japji; the word also means a stair step.

carryVoice: Your line: many forms. A ballad, a stair and a couplet can all live inside one book. A week of the page, closed.

sources.ref: the forms named in the Granth's headings: shabad, ashtpadi (e.g. the Sukhmani, Ang 262 on), chhant, var (e.g. Asa di Var, saloks with pauris, Ang 462 on), pauri (the Japji), salok
